symptom: Docker useradd on Debian overlay can stall all guest execs

reproduction.method: Original unmodified shell script run three times on an APFS copy-on-write clone of the frozen Debian environment. Original manifest unchanged during cloning; source environment and project data untouched during development acceptance.
reproduction.candidate_note: First candidate contains immutable device, separated directory stat and copy-up lock-order changes. Final two single-guard limit checks and test-only additions are accepted by final shared suites; final installed stable is rechecked separately.

cause.reader: FileEpoch prepare_open -> inode read -> stat_node_fields -> mount device -> filesystem read
cause.writer: rename_at -> filesystem write -> overlay checkpoint -> inode write
cause.effect: The reader is the kernel owner during cohort preparation, so its lock wait also blocks unrelated guest exec dispatch.

audit.finding: Filesystem lock under inode read during scalar stat
audit.fix: Retain immutable mount device identity; scalar stat has no namespace acquisition

audit.finding: Directory link counting acquires filesystem under scalar inode guard, then re-enters lookup under namespace guard
audit.fix: Release scalar inode guard; count children in filesystem -> inode order; release guards before pseudo lookups

audit.finding: Merged inode write then upper filesystem read opposes upper checkpoint
audit.fix: Acquire upper filesystem before inode; drop filesystem before bulk copy/sync; retain original capacity policy with byte-account snapshot

audit.finding: Two read acquisitions in the same expression can recursively wait behind a queued filesystem writer
audit.fix: Use one scoped read guard for each limit check

audit.finding: Existing explicit inode drop precedes checkpoint; object metadata transactions retained

audit.path: hostfs identity publication, reverse lookup and filesystem sync
audit.finding: Scopes already release inode guards before filesystem publication or take filesystem first

apple.vfs_method: 462 passing final suite plus the separately passing final copy-up regression; production code unchanged for test-only addition

native_linux.vfs_method: Final VFS suite plus new copy-up regression; unchanged ABI/kernel results reused

validation.regression_before: Forced namespace writer correctly fails old device-lock path within the test deadline; forced guard is released and reader joined before assertion

limits: Scoped VFS lock-order source audit, not proof of a globally acyclic runtime lock graph.
No new coordinator, service thread, global lock, try-lock polling or guest errno.
Original report/archive and project data are not redistributed; only derived technical findings and minimal reproduction results are recorded.
